'''''Phyllostachys aureosulcata''''', the '''yellow groove bamboo''', is a species of [[bamboo]] in the family [[Poaceae]].<ref name=POWO>{{cite taxon |POWO |id=415984-1 |title=''Phyllostachys aureosulcata'' McClure |access-date=March 17, 2026}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{Catalogue of Life |id= 6VFPD |title=''Phyllostachys aureosulcata'' McClure |access-date=March 17, 2026}}</ref> It is native to the [[Zhejiang Province]] of China. It is a running [[bamboo]] with a distinctive yellow stripe in the [[culm (botany)|culm]] groove (or [[Sulcus (anatomy)|sulcus]]) that is often grown as an [[Ornamental plant|ornamental]].<ref name=bamboogarden>{{cite web|url= http://www.bamboogarden.com/Phyllostachys%20aureosulcata.html| title= Bamboo Garden - ''Phyllostachys aureosulcata''| accessdate= 2009-07-02}}</ref><ref name=efloras>{{cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242337528| title= Phyllostachys aureosulcata in Flora of China|accessdate=2009-07-02}}</ref>

==Description==
This bamboo grows to an expected height of {{convert|9|m|ft|abbr=off|sp=us}} with a culm [[diameter]] of {{convert|4|cm|in|abbr=on}}.<ref name=efloras/> In areas where the average [[winter]] minimum temperature is above -15°[[Celsius scale|C]] (5°[[Fahrenheit scale|F]]), it may grow to a maximum height of {{convert|14|m|ft|abbr=off|sp=us}} with a diameter of {{convert|6.5|cm|in|abbr=on}}.<ref name=lewis>{{cite web| url= http://www.lewisbamboo.com/yellowgr.html| title= Lewis Bamboo - ''Phyllostachys aureosulcata'' (Yellow Groove Bamboo)| accessdate= 2011-05-24}}</ref> The typical form of this [[species]] has dark green culms with a yellow groove.<ref name=bamboogarden/> Culm sheath colors appear purple-green usually striped with yellow.<ref name=efloras/> Lower portions of the upright culms occasionally bend in a [[zigzag]] pattern.<ref name=boog-spectabilis>{{cite web | url= http://www.bamboogarden.com/Phyllostachys%20aureosulcata%20%27Spectabilis%27.htm | title= Bamboo Garden - ''Phyllostachys aureosulcata'' 'Spectabilis' | accessdate= 2009-07-02 | archive-date= 2021-12-19 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211219190250/http://bamboogarden.com/Phyllostachys%20aureosulcata%20%27Spectabilis%27.htm | url-status= dead }}</ref>

[[File:PhyllostachysAureosulcata.jpg|thumb|''P. aureosulcata'' foliage]]

==Distribution==
This bamboo grows in areas ranging from [[subtropical]] to warm [[temperate]] and tolerates low winter temperatures better than most bamboos, being one of the hardiest bamboos in the [[genus]] ''[[Phyllostachys]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.needmorebamboo.com/hardiness.html |title=Hardiness ratings |accessdate=2012-06-19 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120619041642/http://www.needmorebamboo.com/hardiness.html |archivedate=June 19, 2012 }}</ref> Outside its natural range and areas where the coldest month has mean temperatures of below {{convert|-4|°C|°F|abbr=on}}, the leaves of ''P. aureosulcata'' may not be evergreen and may turn beige and fall off.{{Citation needed|reason=source needed for this sentence|date=May 2014}}

In areas with severely cold winters (USDA [[hardiness zone]] 5 or colder) in the northern parts of the US, northern Asia, and northern Europe, all growth above ground will die back every winter if temperatures remain below {{convert|-18|°C|°F|abbr=on}} for extended periods {{Citation needed|reason=source needed for this phrase|date=May 2014}} but will regrow in the spring to {{convert|1.8|to|2.4|m|ft|abbr=off|sp=us}} tall.<ref name=lewis/>

''Phyllostachys aureosulcata'' is a popular bamboo in the warmer areas of the United States, Europe, Asia, and parts of Australia. In China it is cultivated and found in Beijing and the provinces [[Henan]], [[Jiangsu]] and [[Zhejiang]].<ref name=efloras/>

==Name==
The culm coloration inspires this bamboo's common name of "yellow groove bamboo" and [[botanical name]] of ''aureosulcata''.<ref name=crc-grasses>{{cite book| title= CRC World Dictionary of Grasses| author= Umberto Quattrocchi| year= 2006| page= 1705| publisher= CRC| isbn= 978-0-8493-1303-5}}</ref> The all-green cultivar 'Alata' is also known as "crookstem bamboo" due to its characteristic culm bends common to this species.<ref name=boog-alata/>

==Usage==
Cultivated mainly as an ornamental, this species is also among the best for edible [[Bamboo shoot|shoot]] production, being free of acrid flavor even when raw.<ref name=crc-grasses/> An aggressive spreader, its dense upright growth makes a good [[hedge]] or privacy screen.<ref name=lewis/><ref name=crc-grasses/>

===Cultivars and Forms===
[[File:Bamboo shoot-phyllostachys aureosulcata lama temple-jxc94c.jpg|thumb|Young shoot of ''Phyllostachys aureosulcata'' cv. 'Lama Temple']]
Several [[form (botany)|forms]] and [[cultivar]]s of this species exist in a variety of culm color patterns. ''P. aureosulcata'' f. ''spectabilis'' reverses the colors of the typical form with yellow culms and a green sulcus.<ref name=boog-spectabilis/> This form has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Phyllostachys aureosulcata'' f. ''spectabilis''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/198411/Phyllostachys-aureosulcata-f-spectabilis/Details | access-date = 6 February 2021}}</ref> The form ''aureocaulis''<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Phyllostachys aureosulcata'' f. | url-status= dead
}}</ref><ref name=boog-lama>{{cite web

A sport of ''spectabilis'' called 'Argus' shares the same robust growth qualities and color as ''spectabilis'' but with additional green vertical stripes scattered around the whole [[circumference]] of each culm.<ref name=whittaker/>
The all green form 'Alata' lacks any yellow culm coloring.<ref name=boog-alata>{{cite web
| url= http://www.bamboogarden.com/Phyllostachys%20aureosulcata%20%27Alata%27.html

In [[Spring (season)|spring]], yellow portions of new ''aureosulcata'' culms that receive direct [[sunlight]] during the early cool hours of the day can develop a red tint or magenta blush that lasts for a couple months.<ref name=boog-spectabilis/><ref name=boog-aureocaulis/><ref name=boog-lama/><ref name=whittaker/><ref name=boog-harbin-inversa/>
